title: Reference PCA and study projection

blocks.what_we_do: Fit PCs in the reference and project both datasets onto the same axes.
blocks.why: A joint PCA can be pulled towards a much larger study group. Projection fixes the reference axes first. The same reference allele frequencies, allele weights and standardisation must then be used for reference and study scores. Scaling and signs of PCs are arbitrary; compare patterns on the same scoring scale. We disable mean imputation so missingness remains visible in the scoring denominator.
blocks.you_need: Shared audited sites from 5.3 and the full 4.6 fileset.
blocks.command:
```{r s5-4}
reference <- file.path(cfg$data_dir, "pca_reference", "ref1000g_grch38")
common <- guided_path(cfg, "5.2", "common.txt")
fit <- guided_path(cfg, "5.4", "reference")
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", reference, "--extract", common, "--freq", "--pca", "10", "allele-wts", "--out", fit))
weights <- guided_table(paste0(fit, ".eigenvec.allele"))
id_column <- match("ID", names(weights)); allele_column <- match("A1", names(weights))
first_pc <- match("PC1", names(weights))
score <- c("--read-freq", paste0(fit, ".afreq"), "--score", paste0(fit, ".eigenvec.allele"),
  id_column, allele_column, "header-read", "no-mean-imputation", "variance-standardize",
  "--score-col-nums", paste0(first_pc, "-", first_pc + 9L))
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", reference, "--extract", common, score, "--out", guided_path(cfg, "5.4", "ref_scores")))
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "4.6"), "--extract", common, score, "--out", guided_path(cfg, "5.4", "study_scores")))
guided_artifact_checkpoint(cfg, "5.4", c(paste0(fit, c(".afreq", ".eigenvec", ".eigenval", ".eigenvec.allele")), paste0(guided_path(cfg, "5.4", "ref_scores"), ".sscore"), paste0(guided_path(cfg, "5.4", "study_scores"), ".sscore")), parent = "5.2")
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile data/course/pca_reference/ref1000g_grch38 --extract results/guided/s5-2_common.txt --freq --pca 10 allele-wts --out results/guided/s5-4_reference --threads 2 --memory 2048
bin/plink2 --pfile data/course/pca_reference/ref1000g_grch38 --extract results/guided/s5-2_common.txt --read-freq results/guided/s5-4_reference.afreq --score results/guided/s5-4_reference.eigenvec.allele 2 5 header-read no-mean-imputation variance-standardize --score-col-nums 6-15 --out results/guided/s5-4_ref_scores --threads 2 --memory 2048
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s4-6_state --extract results/guided/s5-2_common.txt --read-freq results/guided/s5-4_reference.afreq --score results/guided/s5-4_reference.eigenvec.allele 2 5 header-read no-mean-imputation variance-standardize --score-col-nums 6-15 --out results/guided/s5-4_study_scores --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--extract` retains audited shared sites; `--freq` writes reference frequencies. `--pca 10 allele-wts` computes ten axes and allele weights. `--read-freq` supplies the same frequencies to both projections. `--score` names the weights and the one-based ID/A1 columns (2 and 5 here); `header-read` uses the header, `no-mean-imputation` avoids mean-filling missing calls, and `variance-standardize` uses frequency-scaled genotypes. `--score-col-nums 6-15` selects PC1 to PC10. The R command derives column numbers from the actual header. `--pfile` reads the specified native genotype set; `--out` names reports. `--threads 2` limits worker threads. `--memory 2048` sets the workspace budget in MiB.
blocks.expected_result:
Reference eigenvectors/eigenvalues, allele weights and two `.sscore` files with PC1_AVG through PC10_AVG. The study projection contains 1,844 samples.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and instructor reference counts passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Why must the study projection use reference frequencies rather than recomputing standardisation from the study alone?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

Otherwise the two sets of scores would not use the same coordinate system.

</details>
